action: Treat unexpected SMS claiming a traffic fine as fraud: do not follow the link or pay, and check with the police through official channels.
date_note: The date of the stop is not given; ZATAZ's page was last updated on 19 November. Investigators began on 17 July 2026.
exec: Fake-base-station SMS fraud was traced and stopped by Hungarian police, per ZATAZ.
geo_basis: place where the car was intercepted, as stated by the source
plain: Hungarian police stopped a car in Pécs carrying a fake mobile base station that sent scam texts posing as the police about a traffic offence.
summary: ZATAZ reports that Hungarian police intercepted a car in Pécs with an SMS blaster, a fake base station, on the rear seat. The investigation began on 17 July 2026 after a mobile operator reported radio anomalies. Messages signed "RENDORSEG" claimed a traffic offence and sent recipients to a fraudulent payment site. Investigators identified nine victims with losses of 4,802,333 HUF; the driver is a 27-year-old Chinese national.
title: Hungarian police stop car with SMS blaster used for fake traffic-fine texts

validation.note: Read the ZATAZ article, which cites the Hungarian police; the police page it links was not opened.
